chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from al-Qasim ibn Burayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

In the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'Whoever marries off a woman who has a defect that she concealed from him and did not clarify to her husband, then he is entitled to the dowry for what he made permissible of her private part, and the amount the man gave her is upon the one who married her off and did not clarify.'

key_terms.تَدْلِيس: Concealment of a defect in marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry when a wife conceals a defect from her husband?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *tadlis* (deception) in marriage contracts, attributing the ruling to Imam Ali (AS) to highlight its foundational status in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that the husband retains the full dowry (*sadaq*) as compensation for the enjoyment of the body, while the intermediary who arranged the marriage and concealed the defect bears the financial liability for the dowry he presented. This ruling underscores the importance of transparency in marital transactions and the specific accountability of matchmakers in Shia legal tradition.
